title: Greeks arrive
hookLine: Alexander reaches the land, and Greek culture spreads

lines: THE EARTH WAS QUIET BEFORE HIM.
THE STORM PASSES. THE CULTURE STAYS.
cards: The first book of Maccabees opens at a gallop. Alexander, son of Philip, the Macedonian, comes out of the land the book calls Chettiim, defeats Darius, king of the Persians.

He takes cities, kills kings, and goes to the ends of the earth, until, in the King James words, "the earth was quiet before him." Soon he falls sick, knows he is dying, and divides his kingdom among his servants.
He reigned twelve years, the book says. A storm that passes. But what he left behind did not pass: Greek language, Greek cities, Greek ways of living arrive in the land of Israel and stay.

teach.b: The Talmud, in tractate Yoma, tells the meeting as a legend. Alexander's army is marching toward Jerusalem.

The high priest, Shimon the Righteous, puts on his priestly garments and, with the city's leaders carrying torches, walks all night to meet him. When Alexander sees him, the conqueror gets down from his chariot and bows.
His men are shocked. Alexander explains: this is the face I see before me when I win my battles. The Temple is spared.
Two worlds meet, and the surprise is who bows.
Shimon the Righteous is the man Pirkei Avot names right after the Great Assembly, the one who said the world stands on three things: Torah, service, and acts of loving-kindness.
So the legend puts the heir of the chain face to face with the man who conquered the world. But meeting isn't always bowing.

teach.h: A PLACE OF EXERCISE IN JERUSALEM.
teach.b: In the first book of Maccabees, some in Israel say, let's make a covenant with the nations around us, and they build a place of exercise in Jerusalem after the customs of the nations. The book is not pleased.

Two cultures meet, and the meeting goes in every direction: respect, borrowing, worry, conflict. The Hebrew name for Greece, Yavan, turns up in the book of Daniel too: the kingdom of Yavan comes after Persia.
The question for the next few days: how do you live inside someone else's culture and stay yourself?

how: Jewish students learn the saying of Shimon the Righteous in Pirkei Avot, that the world stands on Torah, service and acts of loving-kindness, and the Talmud's legend of his meeting with Alexander is told in study of the Second Temple period.

o: Greek language and ways settling into the land of Israel
Jews leaving Judah to live in the cities of Greece
Greek armies destroying the Temple in Jerusalem

p: the high priest who met him

s: in the Talmud's legend, the high priest bows to Alexander
it's the other way around: Alexander gets down from his chariot and bows to Shimon the Righteous.
the first book of Maccabees says Alexander reigned twelve years
it tells his whole career in a few verses, then he falls sick and divides his kingdom.
Shimon the Righteous taught that the world stands on three things
Torah, service, and acts of loving-kindness, in Pirkei Avot.

games.q: you're Shimon the Righteous. a conquering army is marching on Jerusalem. what do you do?
o: bar the gates and prepare to fight.
put on the priestly garments and walk out to meet him.
flee the city with the Temple treasures.
games.why: in the Talmud's legend he walks out through the night in his priestly garments, and Alexander gets down and bows.

practice: Walk through an ordinary day in your mind, the gym, a class, a word you use, and find one thing you suspect came from Greek culture; if you're not sure, just hold the question.
Then find one thing from your own family, people or tradition, and let both sit side by side without picking a winner. If you pray, use words from your tradition for the places you live.

wordCard.voice: Greeks arrive. Alexander sweeps through, and Greek language and ways of life settle into the land of Israel. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Yavan, the Bible's name for Greece, as in the book of Daniel.

carryVoice: Your line: two cultures meet. Sometimes the meeting is a bow, sometimes a quarrel. See you tomorrow.
